assessment.title: Mathematics 1 Calibration

studentIntro.heading: Find your starting level
studentIntro.supportingText: The questions change pace and difficulty, just like a real admissions test. If one feels difficult, make your best choice and keep moving.

instructions: Choose one answer for every question.
Diagrams are not intended to be measured.
Do not show difficulty labels, specification references, correct answers, or diagnostic tags during the test.

rules: Use equal aspect ratio for Euclidean geometry.
Use MathText for mathematical labels and DejaVu Sans for prose labels.
Leave at least 18 rendered pixels between labels and geometry.
Do not use perspective distortion to imply a measurable length.
Use colour-independent differences: labels, outlines, dashes, and fill values must remain distinguishable in grayscale.
Crop with generous whitespace; no title inside the image.
Provide descriptive alt text from visualSpec.altText.

researchBasis: UAT-UK ESAT Content Specification for assessment in October 2026 and January 2027
UAT-UK 2022 and 2023 NSAA Mathematics papers for pacing and question-writing style
assessment.originalityStatement: Every question below is original. None reproduces an official ESAT, NSAA, or ENGAA question.

questions.stemMarkdown: \(ABCD\) is a square of side \(12\text{ cm}\). The points \(E,F,G,H\) are the midpoints of its sides. The circle touches all four sides of the square \(EFGH\). What fraction of the area of \(ABCD\) lies inside the circle?

visualSpec.altText: A square ABCD. The midpoints E, F, G and H are joined to form a rotated inner square. A circle is inscribed in the inner square. The outer side length is 12 centimetres.

questions.solutionMarkdown: The diagonals of square \(EFGH\) are both \(12\), so its area is \(\tfrac12\times12\times12=72\). Its side length is \(6\sqrt2\), so the radius of its incircle is \(3\sqrt2\). The circle has area \(\pi(3\sqrt2)^2=18\pi\). Therefore the required fraction is \(18\pi/144=\boxed{\pi/8}\).
questions.fastInsight: The midpoint square has half the outer area, and its incircle has radius half its side.

questions.stemMarkdown: A time-lapse camera takes exactly four images per minute. Each image uses \(6.0\text{ MB}\) of storage. The camera runs for \(2.5\) hours. How much storage does it use? Assume \(1000\text{ MB}=1\text{ GB}\).
questions.solutionMarkdown: There are \(2.5\times60=150\) minutes, so the camera takes \(150\times4=600\) images. These use \(600\times6.0=3600\text{ MB}=\boxed{3.6\text{ GB}}\).
questions.fastInsight: Convert the running time to minutes before multiplying by the image rate.

questions.internalTitle: Light beam through a parabolic arch
questions.stemMarkdown: The cross-section of an arch is modelled by \(y=kx(8-x)\), where distances are in metres. The arch passes through \((2,12)\). A horizontal light beam at \(y=9\) meets the arch at \(P\) and \(Q\). What is the horizontal distance \(PQ\)?

visualSpec.altText: A downward-opening parabolic arch crosses the ground at x equals 0 and x equals 8 and passes through the point 2, 12. A horizontal line y equals 9 intersects the arch at P and Q.

questions.solutionMarkdown: Using \((2,12)\), \(12=k(2)(6)\), so \(k=1\). At the beam, \(x(8-x)=9\), giving \(x^2-8x+9=0\). Hence \(x=4\pm\sqrt7\). The horizontal separation is therefore \((4+\sqrt7)-(4-\sqrt7)=\boxed{2\sqrt7\text{ m}}\).
questions.fastInsight: The two roots are symmetric about x = 4, so their separation is twice the square-root term.

questions.stemMarkdown: The intensities of the red and blue lights in a display are initially in the ratio \(3:2\). The red intensity is increased by \(20\%\), while the blue intensity is decreased by \(10\%\). What is the new ratio of red intensity to blue intensity?
questions.solutionMarkdown: Represent the original intensities by \(3u\) and \(2u\). The new intensities are \(1.2(3u)=3.6u\) and \(0.9(2u)=1.8u\). Thus the new ratio is \(3.6:1.8=\boxed{2:1}\).
questions.fastInsight: Apply the percentage multipliers to the two parts separately.

questions.stemMarkdown: Each spinner has four equal sectors. The two spinners are spun independently and the two numbers are added. What is the probability that the total is a prime number?

visualSpec.altText: Two circular spinners, each divided into four equal sectors. Spinner X has sectors labelled 1, 2, 2 and 3. Spinner Y has sectors labelled 1, 2, 3 and 4.

questions.solutionMarkdown: There are \(4\times4=16\) equally likely sector pairs. With \(X=1\), three totals are prime; with either sector labelled \(2\), two totals are prime, contributing \(2+2\); and with \(X=3\), two totals are prime. This gives \(3+2+2+2=9\) favourable pairs, so the probability is \(\boxed{9/16}\).
questions.fastInsight: Use a 4 by 4 possibility grid and remember that the two sectors labelled 2 are distinct outcomes.

questions.stemMarkdown: A 3D printer uses uniform plastic filament with cross-sectional area \(0.40\text{ mm}^2\). Filament enters the printer at \(75\text{ mm s}^{-1}\) for \(10\) minutes. The plastic has density \(1.2\text{ g cm}^{-3}\). Assuming no plastic is wasted, what mass of plastic is used?
questions.solutionMarkdown: In \(10\) minutes there are \(600\) seconds, so the filament length is \(75\times600=45000\text{ mm}\). Its volume is \(0.40\times45000=18000\text{ mm}^3=18\text{ cm}^3\). The mass is therefore \(1.2\times18=\boxed{21.6\text{ g}}\).
questions.fastInsight: Area multiplied by length gives volume; convert cubic millimetres to cubic centimetres before using the density.

questions.stemMarkdown: A positive number \(x\) satisfies \(x+\dfrac1x=3\). What is the value of \(\dfrac{x^3}{x^6+1}\)?
questions.solutionMarkdown: Divide the numerator and denominator by \(x^3\): \(\dfrac{x^3}{x^6+1}=\dfrac1{x^3+x^{-3}}\). Also, \((x+x^{-1})^3=x^3+x^{-3}+3(x+x^{-1})\). Therefore \(27=x^3+x^{-3}+9\), so \(x^3+x^{-3}=18\). The required value is \(\boxed{1/18}\).
questions.fastInsight: Rewrite the requested fraction before trying to solve for x.

questions.stemMarkdown: Six drone lap times, in seconds, are listed in increasing order: \(42,\ 45,\ x,\ x+2,\ 51,\ 60\). Their mean is one second greater than their median. What is the value of \(x\)?
questions.solutionMarkdown: The median is \(\frac{x+(x+2)}2=x+1\). The mean is \(\frac{42+45+x+(x+2)+51+60}{6}=\frac{x+100}{3}\). Since the mean is one greater than the median, \(\frac{x+100}{3}=x+2\). Thus \(x+100=3x+6\), giving \(\boxed{x=47}\).
questions.fastInsight: For six ordered values, the median is the mean of the third and fourth values.

questions.stemMarkdown: The line \(AT\) is tangent to the circle at \(A\). The points \(A,B,C\) lie on the circle, \(AB=AT\), and \(\angle ATB=70^\circ\). What is \(\angle ACB\)?

visualSpec.altText: A circle through A, B and C has a tangent AT at A. Segments AB and AT are marked equal. Triangle ABT lies beside the circle and the angle ATB is 70 degrees.

questions.solutionMarkdown: Since \(AB=AT\), triangle \(ABT\) is isosceles, so \(\angle ABT=\angle ATB=70^\circ\). Hence \(\angle BAT=180^\circ-140^\circ=40^\circ\). By the alternate segment theorem, the angle between tangent \(AT\) and chord \(AB\) equals \(\angle ACB\). Therefore \(\angle ACB=\boxed{40^\circ}\).
questions.fastInsight: First use the isosceles triangle; then transfer its angle using the tangent–chord theorem.

questions.stemMarkdown: Let \(x=\sqrt3+\sqrt2\). What is the value of \(x^2+\dfrac1{x^2}\)?
questions.solutionMarkdown: Because \((\sqrt3+\sqrt2)(\sqrt3-\sqrt2)=1\), we have \(x^{-1}=\sqrt3-\sqrt2\). Therefore \(x+x^{-1}=2\sqrt3\). Squaring gives \(x^2+2+x^{-2}=12\), so \(x^2+x^{-2}=\boxed{10}\).
questions.fastInsight: The reciprocal of x is its conjugate because the product of the conjugates is 1.

questions.stemMarkdown: Sculptures \(X\) and \(Y\) are mathematically similar. The surface area of \(Y\) is \(44\%\) greater than the surface area of \(X\). The material used for \(Y\) has a density \(37.5\%\) lower than the material used for \(X\). What is \(\dfrac{\text{mass of }Y}{\text{mass of }X}\)?
questions.solutionMarkdown: The surface-area ratio is \(1.44=36/25\), so the linear scale factor is \(6/5\). The volume ratio is therefore \((6/5)^3=216/125\). A \(37.5\%\) reduction gives density ratio \(62.5\%=5/8\). Hence the mass ratio is \(\frac{216}{125}\times\frac58=\boxed{\frac{27}{25}}\).
questions.fastInsight: Surface area determines the square of the scale factor; mass is density multiplied by volume.

questions.stemMarkdown: A rectangular light wall grows in the pattern shown. Each dot represents one light. The pattern continues in the same way. What is the first stage containing more than \(280\) lights?

visualSpec.altText: Stage 1 is a grid of 2 rows by 4 columns of lights. Stage 2 is 3 rows by 5 columns. Stage 3 is 4 rows by 6 columns.

questions.solutionMarkdown: At Stage \(n\), the grid has \(n+1\) rows and \(n+3\) columns, so it contains \((n+1)(n+3)\) lights. Stage \(14\) has \(15\times17=255\) lights, while Stage \(15\) has \(16\times18=288\) lights. Therefore the first stage above \(280\) is \(\boxed{\text{Stage }15}\).
questions.fastInsight: Identify the row and column rules separately, then check the two stages around the threshold.

questions.stemMarkdown: Box \(A\) contains two gold counters and one blue counter. Box \(B\) contains one gold counter and three blue counters. A fair coin is used to choose a box, then two counters are drawn from that box without replacement. The two counters are the same colour. What is the probability that Box \(A\) was chosen?

visualSpec.altText: Box A contains counters G, G and B. Box B contains counters G, B, B and B. G means gold and B means blue.

questions.solutionMarkdown: For Box \(A\), a matching pair must be the two gold counters, so \(P(\text{match}|A)=1/3\). For Box \(B\), a matching pair must be two of the three blue counters, so \(P(\text{match}|B)=\binom32/\binom42=1/2\). The boxes are initially equally likely, so \(P(A|\text{match})=\frac{1/3}{1/3+1/2}=\boxed{2/5}\).
questions.fastInsight: Because the prior box probabilities are equal, compare only the two matching-pair probabilities.

questions.stemMarkdown: The points \(A=(-2,1)\) and \(B=(6,5)\). The point \(P\) lies on \(AB\) such that \(AP:PB=3:1\). The line through \(P\) perpendicular to \(AB\) meets the \(x\)-axis at \(Q\). What are the coordinates of \(Q\)?

visualSpec.altText: Coordinate axes show A at negative 2, 1 and B at 6, 5. P divides AB in the ratio 3 to 1. A perpendicular from P meets the x-axis at the unnumbered point Q.

questions.solutionMarkdown: From \(A\) to \(B\) the displacement is \((8,4)\). Since \(AP:PB=3:1\), \(P=A+\frac34(8,4)=(4,4)\). The gradient of \(AB\) is \(4/8=1/2\), so the perpendicular gradient is \(-2\). Its equation through \(P\) is \(y-4=-2(x-4)\). Setting \(y=0\) gives \(x=6\), hence \(Q=\boxed{(6,0)}\).
questions.fastInsight: Find P by taking three quarters of the displacement from A to B, then use the negative reciprocal gradient.

questions.stemMarkdown: A tiny robot starts at vertex \(A\) of a solid cuboid and must reach the opposite vertex \(G\) while remaining on the surface. The cuboid has edge lengths \(3\text{ cm}\), \(5\text{ cm}\), and \(6\text{ cm}\). What is the length of the shortest possible route?

geometry.hiddenEdges: omit if they cross a visible face in the chosen projection

visualSpec.altText: A cuboid has edge lengths 3, 5 and 6 centimetres. A is one vertex and G is the opposite vertex. The required route must stay on the surface.

questions.solutionMarkdown: Unfolding two adjacent faces gives three essentially different rectangles. Their corner-to-corner lengths are \(\sqrt{(3+5)^2+6^2}=10\), \(\sqrt{(3+6)^2+5^2}=\sqrt{106}\), and \(\sqrt{(5+6)^2+3^2}=\sqrt{130}\). The least is therefore \(\boxed{10\text{ cm}}\). The body diagonal \(\sqrt{70}\) passes through the solid and is not a permitted surface route.
questions.fastInsight: Unfold the two faces crossed by a route into one rectangle; there are only three pairings to compare.
